security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on base.group_system field groups guarding nuvei_site_identifier and nuvei_secret_key (the checksum key). nuvei_merchant_identifier is the only non-system-restricted credential field.

views.note: xml_loc=54 across three data files: payment_provider_views.xml inherits payment.payment_provider_form to add Merchant Identifier / Site Identifier / Secret Key (password) fields, invisible unless code=='nuvei'; payment_nuvei_templates.xml defines the QWeb redirect_form (a method='post' auto-submit form carrying a 'checksum' hidden input plus every url_params field, targeting the Nuvei PPP purchase.do Cashier); payment_provider_data.xml seeds the provider and wires redirect_form_view_id. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> client-side form POST to the Nuvei PPP hosted Cashier (https://secure.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do | https://ppp-test.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do)
behavioral_notes.observation: Nuvei uses the SafeCharge PPP (Payment Page / hosted Cashier) and -- unlike Stripe/Mollie -- makes NO server-to-server REST call: there is no requests import, no _build_request_url, no _send_api_request override anywhere in the module. Instead _get_specific_rendering_values assembles a flat dict of url_params (merchant_id=nuvei_merchant_identifier, merchant_site_id=nuvei_site_identifier, currency, total_amount/item_amount_1 rounded DOWN to currency decimals -- or 0 decimals for const.INTEGER_METHODS like webpay, item_name_1/invoice_id=reference, payment_method=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING.get(payment_method_code) with payment_method_mode='filter' [e.g. card->cc_card, pix->apmgw_PIX, boleto->apmgw_BOLETO, oxxopay->apmgw_OXXO_PAY, pse->apmgw_PSE, spei->apmgw_SPEI, webpay->apmgw_Webpay], billing address/email/phone [phone _phone_format-validated], first_name[:30]/last_name[:40] [const.FULL_NAME_METHODS like boleto require both names, else UserError], time_stamp from create_date, version '4.0.0', user_token_id=uuid4(), and success/pending/back/error/notify URLs pointing at the Odoo routes). It computes a checksum over those params and returns {api_url=_nuvei_get_api_url(), checksum, url_params}; the QWeb redirect_form then auto-POSTs them (checksum as a dedicated hidden input) to the live or test purchase.do Cashier. The hosted-Cashier handoff, the form-POST (not API) flow, and the SafeCharge endpoints are invisible to Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._nuvei_calculate_signature / _nuvei_get_api_url -> SHA-256 checksum auth (outbound + inbound) and live/test endpoint selection
behavioral_notes.observation: _nuvei_get_api_url returns https://secure.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do when provider.state=='enabled' else the ppp-test.safecharge.com test Cashier -- live/test is driven by the provider state, not separate keys. _nuvei_calculate_signature(data, incoming=) implements Nuvei's checksum scheme: it concatenates string values of selected keys, prepends the nuvei_secret_key, and SHA-256-hexdigests the result -- key = nuvei_secret_key; signing_string = key + ''.join(str(data[k]) for k in keys). For OUTBOUND signing (incoming=False) it concatenates ALL of the outgoing data.keys() in dict order (the checksum sent on the redirect form). For INBOUND verification (incoming=True) it concatenates exactly const.SIGNATURE_KEYS in order -- ['totalAmount','currency','responseTimeStamp','PPP_TransactionID','Status','productId'] -- prepended with the secret. So the shared secret is a checksum key, NOT a Bearer token; there is no Authorization header anywhere. The SHA-256 scheme, the differing key sets per direction, and the state-driven endpoint are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: NuveiController.nuvei_webhook (/payment/nuvei/webhook DMN) + nuvei_return_from_checkout (/payment/nuvei/return) -> _verify_signature BEFORE _process (checksum or access-token), reference via invoice_id
behavioral_notes.observation: Both routes locate the tx via _search_by_reference('nuvei', data) (routing through _extract_reference -> data['invoice_id']; the return route falls back to {'invoice_id': tx_ref} when Nuvei sends nothing back) and call the staticmethod _verify_signature BEFORE _process('nuvei', data). _verify_signature has two branches: (1) when an error_access_token is present (the cancel/parse-error 'leaving' flow, where Nuvei returns NO checksum), it validates payment_utils.check_access_token(error_access_token, reference) and raises werkzeug Forbidden on mismatch; (2) otherwise (payment went through) it reads the 'advanceResponseChecksum' field, raises Forbidden if missing, recomputes the expected checksum via provider._nuvei_calculate_signature(payment_data, incoming=True) over const.SIGNATURE_KEYS, and rejects with Forbidden unless tools.consteq (constant-time) matches. The webhook (csrf=False POST DMN) returns 'OK'; the return route (GET) redirects to /payment/status. This dual checksum-or-access-token verification gate is invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates / _extract_amount_data -> Nuvei status -> payment state machine; empty-data 'customer left' handling
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates first handles the empty-data case (user abandoned the Cashier and Nuvei posted nothing): it _set_canceled('The customer left the payment page.') and returns. Otherwise it stores provider_reference = payment_data['TransactionID'], back-resolves the payment.method from payment_data['payment_method'] via _get_from_code(mapping=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING), then reads Status (or fallback ppp_status), lowercases it, and maps via const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING: 'pending' -> _set_pending; 'approved'/'ok' -> _set_done; 'declined'/'error'/'fail' -> _set_error (with Reason/message as the failure reason); missing status -> _set_error; any other value -> logged and _set_error. _extract_amount_data pulls totalAmount/currency and re-uses the INTEGER_METHODS rounding (precision_digits) for the amount check, returning early (None) on empty data. The status->state mapping and the abandoned-payment cancel path are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, checksum key, no SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; endpoints https://ppp-test.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do (test Cashier) and https://secure.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do (live Cashier), both declared in models/payment_provider.py (_nuvei_get_api_url). There is NO outbound REST client (http_call_sites=0, sdk_imports=[]): the only outbound link is the browser auto-POSTing the signed form to the SafeCharge purchase.do Cashier, where card details are entered (the module ships no static/src assets, only description icons -- PCI scope stays with Nuvei). Authenticity is a SHA-256 checksum keyed on nuvei_secret_key (NOT a Bearer token), verified inbound over const.SIGNATURE_KEYS, with an access-token fallback for the no-checksum cancel/leave flow. This form-redirect-plus-checksum acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata; it was established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

extract_frontend.py reports present=false: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates beyond the server-rendered QWeb redirect_form, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. Unlike Stripe/Xendit there is no client-side SDK and no PaymentForm patch: the module relies entirely on the generic 'payment' redirect-with-form-submission flow, and the only template is the server-side auto-submit redirect_form that POSTs the browser (with the checksum + url_params) to Nuvei's hosted Cashier. So gap #3 is effectively empty here -- the browser-side acquirer interaction happens on Nuvei's hosted Cashier page, not in Odoo-shipped JS.

/payment/nuvei/webhook (Nuvei DMN async notification: http POST, csrf=False; verifies advanceResponseChecksum then _process; returns 'OK')

external_integrations.sdk: none (no python SDK, no client-side JS SDK -- card entry on Nuvei's hosted Cashier); no outbound REST client at all (http_call_sites=0)
endpoints: https://ppp-test.safecharge.com/ppp/purchase.do (test PPP Cashier; selected by provider.state via _nuvei_get_api_url)
external_integrations.auth: SHA-256 checksum keyed on nuvei_secret_key (NOT a Bearer token): outbound = SHA256(secret + concat(all outgoing param values)); inbound verify = SHA256(secret + concat(const.SIGNATURE_KEYS values)) compared via consteq against advanceResponseChecksum. nuvei_merchant_identifier + nuvei_site_identifier identify the merchant/site on the form.
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration, but a pure CLIENT-SIDE redirect/form-POST one -- there is no server-to-server REST call. _get_specific_rendering_values signs a flat parameter dict with a SHA-256 checksum (keyed on nuvei_secret_key) and the browser auto-POSTs it to the SafeCharge purchase.do hosted Cashier; settlement returns via a DMN webhook and a redirect-return, each gated by recomputing the checksum (const.SIGNATURE_KEYS) and consteq-comparing advanceResponseChecksum, with a signed access-token fallback for the no-checksum cancel/leave flow. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the SafeCharge purchase.do endpoints, the checksum (non-Bearer) signing, the per-direction key sets (all-params outbound vs SIGNATURE_KEYS inbound), or the access-token cancel-flow fallback are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py. Distinctive vs Mollie (Bearer + re-fetch-by-id) and Stripe (Bearer + HMAC webhook): Nuvei never calls the acquirer server-side -- the whole exchange is a signed browser form-POST plus a checksum-verified return/DMN.

capabilities: Accept Latin-American card / local-method payments via the Nuvei hosted Cashier (redirect/form-POST flow: card, PIX, Boleto, OXXO Pay, PSE, SPEI, Webpay, AstroPay, MercadoPago/Naranja, etc.)
Asynchronous settlement confirmation via a Nuvei DMN webhook plus a checksum-verified redirect-return route
Multi-currency acceptance across const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (ARS, BRL, CLP, COP, MXN, PEN, USD, UYU, CAD)
Per-method amount-format handling (integer-only methods like Webpay) and full-name enforcement for methods like Boleto
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> SHA-256 checksum sign -> browser auto-POST to SafeCharge purchase.do Cashier -> /payment/nuvei/return -> _verify_signature -> _process -> /payment/status
Confirm-Settlement (async DMN): Nuvei -> /payment/nuvei/webhook -> _verify_signature (advanceResponseChecksum consteq) -> _apply_updates status mapping -> _set_pending/_set_done/_set_error
Abandon/Cancel: customer leaves the Cashier -> Nuvei returns no checksum -> error_access_token check -> _apply_updates empty-data path -> _set_canceled('The customer left the payment page.')
Settle: Nuvei status 'approved'/'ok' -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.provider (Nuvei credentials: merchant identifier / site identifier / secret checksum key)
payment.transaction (mapped to a Nuvei Cashier transaction; keyed by invoice_id=reference and provider_reference=TransactionID)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; nuvei_site_identifier and nuvei_secret_key are restricted to base.group_system; nuvei_merchant_identifier is not; everything else inherits payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Webhook/return authenticity: the payment branch must pass _verify_signature -- recompute SHA-256 over const.SIGNATURE_KEYS keyed on nuvei_secret_key and consteq-match advanceResponseChecksum, else HTTP 403 Forbidden; missing checksum is rejected
Cancel/leave flow (no checksum returned) is instead authenticated by a signed access token (payment_utils.check_access_token(error_access_token, reference)); failure -> 403 Forbidden
Live vs test Cashier endpoint chosen by provider.state ('enabled' -> secure.safecharge.com, else ppp-test.safecharge.com), not by separate credentials
Supported currencies bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES; others filtered out by _get_supported_currencies
Amounts rounded DOWN; const.INTEGER_METHODS (e.g. webpay) forced to 0 decimals regardless of currency
const.FULL_NAME_METHODS (e.g. boleto) require both first and last name, else UserError before redirect
Site identifier and secret checksum key gated by base.group_system field groups
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the Nuvei merchant/site ids and secret key)
Nuvei / SafeCharge (external acquirer / PSP for Latin America)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_nuvei is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the payer (cardholder / local-method user) and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Nuvei's (SafeCharge) Latin-American card / local-payment-method network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (merchant id / site id / secret checksum key + currency/payment-method enablement), service provisioning (signing and handing off a Cashier transaction and confirming its status per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the signed browser form-POST to the SafeCharge Cashier plus the checksum-verified DMN/return settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Nuvei realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine. Note the integration is uniquely thin among siblings: a signed redirect form-POST with NO server-to-server REST, settled by a checksum-verified webhook/return.

standard_capabilities: hosted-Cashier redirect acceptance of Latin-American card and local methods via the Nuvei PPP Payment Page (signed browser form-POST to purchase.do; no server-to-server REST)

asynchronous settlement via a DMN webhook plus a redirect-return route, both gated by a SHA-256 checksum (advanceResponseChecksum, consteq), with a signed access-token fallback for the cancel/leave flow

multi-currency acceptance across const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (ARS/BRL/CLP/COP/MXN/PEN/USD/UYU/CAD); integer-only methods (const.INTEGER_METHODS) and full-name-required methods (const.FULL_NAME_METHODS) handled
live/test Cashier endpoint auto-selected by provider.state
automatic provider setup/teardown via post_init_hook setup_provider / uninstall_hook reset_payment_provider
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting payments in Latin America via Nuvei (PIX, Boleto, OXXO, PSE, SPEI, Webpay, cards, etc.)
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
multi-currency LATAM e-commerce where card data should stay on the PSP's hosted Cashier (PCI scope offloaded to Nuvei)
common_gaps: no tokenization (with or without payment / zero-authorization) -- README 'Not implemented'; no payment.token vaulting, no off-session/recurring charge path
no full/partial manual capture (auth-and-settle) and no void operation -- README 'Not implemented'; charge is immediate
no full/partial refund operation -- README 'Not implemented'; no _send_refund_request override (refunds done via the Nuvei dashboard or a downstream module)

no server-to-server API surface at all (no _send_api_request / requests): the only acquirer touchpoint is the signed Cashier form-POST plus the checksum-verified webhook/return, so e.g. server-side status queries or backend operations are not available in-module
no merchant self-onboarding -- merchant id / site id / secret key are entered manually on the provider form
the public-URL requirement for the DMN webhook means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without a correct nuvei_secret_key the checksum verification cannot succeed (events 403'd)
currency support bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES; others filtered out
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
drive_hints: curl -X POST 'https://<host>/payment/nuvei/webhook' --data 'invoice_id=<ref>' (csrf=False, auth=public) with a missing/invalid advanceResponseChecksum -> expect HTTP 403 Forbidden from _verify_signature
Nuvei test cards: VISA 4761344136141390 (up to $99); >$99 requires the 3DS test cards at https://docs.nuvei.com/documentation/integration/testing/testing-cards/ (README testing instructions)

open_questions: Exact Nuvei DMN / Cashier field set returned on success beyond const.SIGNATURE_KEYS + TransactionID/payment_method/Status/Reason, and how advanceResponseChecksum is composed on Nuvei's side relative to the SIGNATURE_KEYS recomputation.

Real-world distribution of Nuvei transaction states and method mix (card vs PIX/Boleto/OXXO/Webpay, etc.), and how often the abandoned-Cashier 'customer left' cancel path fires (no runtime row counts captured).
How refunds/captures/tokenization are handled operationally given none are implemented in-module (likely via the Nuvei dashboard or a downstream module).

Whether instances reliably register the DMN webhook (public URL reachable, correct nuvei_secret_key) vs rely on the redirect-return route, and how duplicate return+DMN notifications are de-duplicated by the payment engine.
